newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday due to the strong performance of the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 9.9 percent from 7.55 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 3.28 million lots from 4.2 million on Tuesday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said institutions borrowed money on the repo market to trade in A shares, pushing up the repo rates on Wednesday.
Rumours that the central government would set up a united national state debt trading market based in Beijing this year kept some major traders sidelined, depressing volume, traders said.
"If A share prices can keep an upward trend in the next few days, the repo rates will continue to rise," one trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Wednesday on a continued technical correction that began on Monday, traders said.
The most active three-year bond maturing in August 1999 fell to 83.45 yuan from 83.70 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell sharply to 960,504 lots from 1.56 million.
Traders said the technical correction was likely to continue for another one or two days but the mid-term trend for the spot market would be good due to strong fundamentals.
